title: Relation between temperature scales (ভিন্ন স্কেলের মাঝে সম্পর্ক)
placement: Book pages 165–166, topic 6.2.1 (ভিন্ন স্কেলের মাঝে সম্পর্ক): next to the relation T_C/100 = (T_K − 273.15)/100 = (T_F − 32)/180 and the four উদাহরণ (C = F at −40°, K = F at 574.59 K, 98.4° F in Celsius, C and K never equal). The page has no picture; this is the one the formulas describe.
description: Three thermometers on one wooden board, the same liquid at the same height in all of them: a Celsius, a Kelvin and a Fahrenheit scale (the book's order, with the formula's two fixed marks 0/100, 273.15/373.15 and 32/212 on the same two levels). The student drags the top of the liquid, or taps the numbered button for the book's four examples (C = F at −40°, K = F at 574.59 K, a healthy body at 98.4° F, C and K never equal); the three readings move together and the two relations T_C = T_K − 273.15° and T_C = 5/9 (T_F − 32°) are worked with the student's own numbers. Then a five-question test. The drawn scale spans −50° to 310° C so that every example fits.
